name: Fix a Force Push Disaster
problem: You or a teammate accidentally ran `git push --force` on the `main` branch, overwriting history and deleting several days of work.

steps.title: Don't panic! Check the reflog
steps.description: Git's reflog records every movement of the HEAD pointer on your local machine. If you had the correct version of `main` locally recently, it's still there.
steps.code:
git reflog

# Look for the last known good state of main before the force push
# It might look like: a1b2c3d HEAD@{5}: pull: Fast-forward

steps.title: Reset to the good state
steps.description: Once you find the hash of the commit before the disaster, hard reset your local `main` branch to it.

steps.title: Force push the fix
steps.description: Now you need to force push again to restore the remote repository to the correct state.

alternatives.title: What if my local reflog doesn't have it?
alternatives.description: If you didn't have the recent code, ask the teammate whose code was deleted. Their local `main` branch or their reflog will have the correct commits. They just need to force push their local branch.
alternatives.code:
# Teammate runs:
git checkout main
git push --force origin main
